args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money (FIN-212)

round_money used ROUND_HALF_UP, contrary to the banker's rounding
required by FIN-212. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so the nightly
tests/test_money.py passes.

args.head: fix/money-banker-rounding
args.title: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but FIN-212 requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail in `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.

## Change
- Switch the rounding mode from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `src/money.py`.
- No other changes.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: passed.
- Expected results: `2.675 -> 2.68` and `2.665 -> 2.66`, as asserted in the test.

## Note
This changes rounding for all callers of `round_money`, so amounts that land exactly on a half-cent will now round to the nearest even cent. This is intended per FIN-212, but please review with that in mind.

I fixed the nightly failure and opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer. I did not merge it, since merging into main needs code-owner approval.

- **Fix:** In `src/money.py`, `round_money` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`. I changed it to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` to match FIN-212 and the test's expectations (2.675 → 2.68, 2.665 → 2.66). The change is one line, committed to `fix/money-banker-rounding`.
- **CI:** Run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed.
- **PR:** https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The first two `open_pr` attempts returned 503 errors and no PR was created. I confirmed that with `list_prs` before using `open_pr_legacy`, which created the PR once.

The PR description notes that the change alters rounding for every caller of `round_money` on exact half-cent amounts. Alex should review with that in mind.

content.text: I'll start by reading the source and the test to see what's expected.

The bug is clear: the docstring and FIN-212 call for ROUND_HALF_EVEN, but the code uses ROUND_HALF_UP. Under half-even, 2.675 → 2.68 (7 is odd, so it rounds to 8) and 2.665 → 2.66 (6 is even), which matches the test. I'll create the branch and commit the one-line fix.
